Step 2

Does almost matching satisfy fixed ends?

Fixed ends require y(0,t)=y(L,t)=0 at every time, not merely a zero crossing now. The original trial y=A sin(ωt−kx)−A sin(ωt+kx)=−2A cos(ωt)sin(kx) automatically fixes only x=0. The right end additionally needs sin(kL)=0, or q=2L/λ=n, n=1,2,…. Only then is this single free-vibration shape a normal mode, with λₙ=2L/n. An incompatible trial can be drawn for inspection, but is not actual motion of a fixed-end string.

White pins/walls: required zero displacement. Cyan dashed line: incompatible trial shape; red ring: its demanded endpoint now; red dashed marker: its nonzero full-cycle endpoint envelope. Only a boundary match receives a green solid curve and nodes. Numerical tolerance handles floating-point error, not a “within2% counts” rule.

Demonstration time t≈0s: trial right-end displacement≈0A; its whole-cycle endpoint amplitude≈0A. A zero now does not mean always zero.

L=6, λ≈4; q=2L/λ≈3. Nearest reachable candidate by wavelength distance: n=3, λₙ≈4; its |q−n|≈0.

Mode n=3: fixed-end conditions hold within floating-point precision. λₙ=2L/n≈4; the endpoint envelope vanishes for the whole cycle. Rounded display does not replace the exact ratio.

The fixed demonstration T=4s shows candidate spatial shapes. Changing λ also changes the illustrative λ/T speed; this is not a frequency sweep of one unchanged physical string. Step3 specifies wave speed before calculating frequency. Failure rules out this single free-mode trial, not every possible forced motion; no forced or off-resonance response is solved here.
